mainTopic: The burials of יוסף and משה: honor, finishing a good deed, and the death and hidden grave of משה
overview: The amud opens by finishing the story of יוסף's coffin traveling beside the holy ארון: יוסף kept everything written in it. The גמרא explains why יוסף's sons and בני ישראל each left his burial to others: to give him more honor. It also explains why he was buried in שכם, and how both משה and בני ישראל get credit for carrying his bones. From this comes a lesson that whoever finishes a good deed gets credit for all of it, while יהודה, who started saving יוסף but did not finish, was lowered and lost his wife and sons. Several teachings about יוסף follow: why he was called 'bones,' why he died before his brothers, how he lowered פרעה's astrologers, and what happened to פוטיפר. The גמרא then turns to the משנה's praise of משה's burial. It explains the words 'רב לך,' learns that צדיקים live out their years to the exact day, and shows how leadership passed to יהושע. Finally it describes how הקב״ה Himself carried משה from נבו in ראובן's land to his grave in גד's land, and how no one knows where that grave is. A story about the Roman government trying to find the grave begins at the end and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: יוסף fulfilled everything written in the Torah
steps.stepSummary: The punchline of the earlier story: יוסף's ארון travels next to the ארון of the Torah because יוסף kept everything written in it.
steps.simpleTranslation: This one (יוסף) fulfilled everything that is written in this one (the Torah in the ארון).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer from the story that came just before this point. People asked why יוסף's coffin travels beside the holy ארון, and the answer is that יוסף kept everything written in what that ארון holds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'this' is used twice and means two different things. The first 'this' is יוסף, who is in his coffin. The second 'this' is what the holy ארון contains. Because יוסף lived by what is written there, it is fitting for the two ארונות to travel side by side.

keyTerms.meaning: this one... in this one (יוסף... in what the ארון holds)
coffin, or the holy ark (the same word is used for both)

steps.confusionAlert: The two uses of 'זה' point to two different things. The first is יוסף, and the second is what is written in the holy ארון.
steps.whatToRemember: יוסף's coffin was honored by traveling next to the holy ארון because he fulfilled what is written in it.

phrases.aramaic: קִיֵּים זֶה כׇּל מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בָּזֶה.
phrases.english: This one fulfilled all that is written in this one.
phrases.notes: The first 'this one' is יוסף in his coffin. The second is what the holy ארון holds.

steps.triggerLanguage: קִיֵּים זֶה כׇּל מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בָּזֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the story about the two ארונות that began before this point.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: יוסף's righteousness earned his coffin a place beside the holy ארון.

steps.title: Wouldn't the people have buried יוסף without משה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that משה had to handle יוסף's bones, quoting a פסוק that says בני ישראל buried him.
steps.simpleTranslation: If משה hadn't dealt with יוסף's bones, wouldn't בני ישראל have dealt with them? After all, it is written: 'And the bones of יוסף, which בני ישראל brought up from Egypt, they buried in שכם.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions why משה had to take care of יוסף's bones himself. It points to a פסוק showing that בני ישראל took care of the burial in the end.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the story praised משה for handling יוסף's bones, as though nobody else would have done it. The פסוק in יהושע says בני ישראל did the burial. So why didn't the people take care of it from the start?

keyTerms.meaning: dealt with it, took care of it
but isn't it written? (introduces a פסוק used as a challenge)

phrases.english: And if Moshe had not dealt with it —
would the Jewish people not have dealt with it?
But isn't it written: "And the bones of Yosef,
which the children of Israel brought up out of Egypt,
they buried in Shechem"!
phrases.notes: יהושע 24:32

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי לָא עֲסִיק בֵּיהּ מֹשֶׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the earlier praise of משה for personally handling יוסף's bones.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that משה had to be the one to handle יוסף's bones
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק says בני ישראל buried יוסף, so they were able and willing to do it. Why did it fall to משה?

steps.title: Wouldn't יוסף's own sons have buried him?
steps.stepSummary: A second, related challenge: even without the whole people, יוסף's descendants should have taken care of him, as the same פסוק shows.
steps.simpleTranslation: And further: if בני ישראל hadn't dealt with him, wouldn't his own sons have dealt with him? After all, it is written: 'And they became an inheritance for the sons of יוסף.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second question. יוסף's own family should have been the first to look after his burial.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק says the burial place became the inheritance of יוסף's sons. That shows his family had a direct connection to the burial. So why did they leave it to the whole people, and the people leave it to משה?

phrases.aramaic: וְתוּ: אִי לָא אִיעֲסַקוּ בֵּיהּ יִשְׂרָאֵל —
phrases.english: And furthermore: if the Jewish people had not dealt with it —
would his sons not have dealt with it?
But isn't it written: "And they became the inheritance of the sons of Yosef"?!
phrases.notes: This is the end of the same פסוק in יהושע 24:32.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ: אִי לָא אִיעֲסַקוּ בֵּיהּ יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second challenge on top of the first, moving down from the whole people to יוסף's own family.
steps.kashyaTarget: Why the burial was handed off by יוסף's sons and by the people
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The burial land belonged to יוסף's sons, so they were the natural ones to bury him. Why did the task move away from them?

steps.title: They stepped back for יוסף's honor
steps.stepSummary: Each group left the burial to someone else so that יוסף would get greater honor: by many rather than few, and by a great person rather than lesser people.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: Leave him. His honor is greater through many people than through a few. And further they said: Leave him. His honor is greater through great people than through lesser ones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers both questions. Nobody was neglecting יוסף. Each group stepped aside on purpose so that he would be honored more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יוסף's sons, a small group, let the whole people handle it, because being buried by many is a greater honor. בני ישראל in turn let משה handle it, because being cared for by a great person is a greater honor than being cared for by ordinary people. Stepping back here was itself a way of showing respect.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two reasons, one for each question. More people give more honor, so the sons stepped back for the people. A greater person gives more honor, so the people stepped back for משה.

phrases.english: They said: Leave him,
phrases.notes: This is יוסף's sons talking, leaving the burial to the whole people.

phrases.english: his honor is greater through the many than through the few.
And furthermore they said: Leave him,
phrases.notes: Now בני ישראל are talking, leaving it to משה.

phrases.english: his honor is greater through the great than through the lesser.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ: הַנִּיחוּ לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers both challenges from steps 2 and 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a reason that explains why the others held back
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed that the sons and the people should have buried יוסף themselves, so handing it to משה looked unnecessary.
steps.terutzMaskana: They held back on purpose so that יוסף would receive the greater honor of being buried by many people and by a great person.

steps.title: Why bury יוסף in שכם?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the פסוק and asks what was special about שכם as יוסף's burial place.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'They buried him in שכם.' What is different about שכם?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the words 'they buried in שכם' and asks why that city was chosen. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the גמרא asks about a new detail of the same פסוק: the place, not the people who did the burial. It assumes the choice of שכם had a reason behind it.

keyTerms.meaning: what is different? why specifically this?

phrases.english: "They buried in Shechem."
What is different about Shechem?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא בִּשְׁכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the פסוק quoted in step 2 to ask about the place of burial.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why שכם was chosen as יוסף's burial place

steps.title: Returning יוסף to where he was taken from
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא explains that יוסף was taken from שכם, so they returned him there, like returning a lost object.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא said: From שכם they stole him, and to שכם we will return what was lost.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא answers the question. They chose שכם because that is where יוסף's troubles began.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His brothers took יוסף away from שכם. Burying him there brings him back to the place he was taken from. The גמרא describes this as returning a lost object to where it belongs.

keyTerms.meaning: his lost object, meaning what was lost

steps.whatToRemember: יוסף was buried in שכם because he was taken from שכם. He was returned to the place he was lost from.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥama, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, said:
From Shechem they stole him,
phrases.notes: His brothers took him away near שכם. See בראשית 37.

phrases.english: and to Shechem we will return his lost one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חָמָא בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא: מִשְּׁכֶם גְּנָבוּהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שכם was chosen because יוסף was taken from there, so he was returned there like a lost object.

steps.title: Two verses disagree about who carried יוסף's bones
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that one פסוק says משה took יוסף's bones, while another says בני ישראל brought them up.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verses contradict each other. It is written: "And משה took the bones of יוסף with him," and it is written: "And the bones of יוסף, which בני ישראל brought up..."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets two פסוקים side by side and shows they seem to clash: who actually took יוסף's bones, משה or בני ישראל?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In שמות the credit goes to משה personally. In יהושע the same act is credited to בני ישראל. Both cannot simply be the whole story, so the גמרא needs to explain how both are true.

keyTerms.meaning: "Etc.": the rest of the פסוק continues

steps.confusionAlert: The פסוק in יהושע was already used in Steps 2 and 3, but here it serves a different question. Earlier the issue was who should have buried יוסף. Now it is a direct clash over who carried the bones.

phrases.english: The verses contradict each other:
It is written: "And Moshe took
the bones of Yosef with him,"
phrases.notes: שמות 13:19

phrases.english: and it is written: "And the bones of Yosef
which the children of Israel brought up, etc."!
phrases.notes: יהושע 24:32

steps.triggerLanguage: קָשׁוּ קְרָאֵי אַהֲדָדֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining why יוסף was buried in שכם, the גמרא raises a new clash between two פסוקים about who carried his bones.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two פסוקים describing who took יוסף's bones out of מצרים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One פסוק credits משה alone and the other credits בני ישראל, so they seem to contradict.

steps.title: The one who finishes a deed gets credit for the whole thing
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא explains that משה started the job and בני ישראל finished it, so the פסוק credits them as if they did all of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא said: Anyone who does a thing and does not finish it, and another person comes and finishes it, the פסוק credits the one who finished it as if he had done the whole thing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא settles the clash between the two פסוקים with a general rule about who gets credit for a deed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה began carrying יוסף's bones but did not finish, since he died before entering ארץ ישראל. בני ישראל completed the burial, so the פסוק in יהושע describes them as the ones who brought the bones up. Both פסוקים are true: משה started the deed, and בני ישראל finished it and received the credit.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק credits him, counts it for him
As if he had done it (all)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a general principle: finishing a מצוה is so important that the finisher gets credit for the whole act. The next two steps build on it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chama son of Rabbi Chanina said:
Anyone who does a thing and does not finish it,
and another comes and finishes it,
the verse credits him
phrases.notes: "Him" means the one who finished, not the one who started.

phrases.english: for having finished it, as if he had done it.

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּל הָעוֹשֶׂה דָּבָר וְלֹא גְּמָרוֹ, וּבָא אַחֵר וּגְמָרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the contradiction raised in Step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Harmonization: both פסוקים are true, each describing a different stage of the deed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only one of them, משה or בני ישראל, could really have taken the bones.
steps.terutzMaskana: משה started the deed and בני ישראל finished it, and the פסוק credits the finishers as if they did the whole thing.

steps.title: Starting without finishing can cost a person his greatness
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר adds that someone who starts a deed and does not finish it is lowered from his high position, and he learns this from יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: They even lower him from his greatness, as it is written: "And it was at that time, that יהודה went down."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר adds a further point to the rule of Step 8. The one who started but did not finish does not just lose the credit; he is also brought down from his greatness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is the word וַיֵּרֶד, "went down," said about יהודה. The idea is that יהודה started to save יוסף but did not finish the job and bring him home. "Going down" is read as being lowered from his position of leadership among his brothers.

keyTerms.meaning: Also, even: adds to what was said before
They lower him, bring him down

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says:
They even lower him from his greatness,
phrases.notes: "Him" is the one who started the deed but didn't finish it.

phrases.english: as it is written: "And it was at that time
that Judah went down."
phrases.notes: בראשית 38:1. The proof rests on the word "went down."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: אַף מוֹרִידִין אוֹתוֹ מִגְּדוּלָּתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on Step 8's rule by adding a consequence for the one who started but did not finish.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who starts a deed and does not finish it is lowered from his greatness, as seen with יהודה.

steps.title: Starting without finishing can even lead to burying one's family
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני adds an even harsher result: such a person buries his wife and children, as happened to יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said: He even buries his wife and his sons, as it is written: "And בת שוע, the wife of יהודה, died..." and it is written: "And ער and אונן died."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמואל בר נחמני adds one more consequence for someone who starts a good deed but does not finish it, again using יהודה as the example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He points to two פסוקים: one telling that יהודה's wife died, and one telling that his sons ער and אונן died. He reads these losses as part of what happened to יהודה for not finishing what he started with יוסף.

keyTerms.meaning: The daughter of שוע, יהודה's wife
ער and אונן, two of יהודה's sons

steps.whatToRemember: Finishing a good deed matters greatly. The one who finishes gets credit for all of it (רבי חמא ברבי חנינא). The one who starts and stops can be lowered from his greatness (רבי אלעזר) and even bury his wife and sons (רבי שמואל בר נחמני), as happened to יהודה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said:
He even buries his wife and his sons,
as it is written: "And the daughter of Shua died,
the wife of Judah, etc."
phrases.notes: בראשית 38:12

phrases.english: and it is written: "And Er and Onan died."
phrases.notes: בראשית 46:12

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר: אַף קוֹבֵר אִשְׁתּוֹ וּבָנָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further and harsher consequence on top of רבי אלעזר's point in Step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who starts a deed and does not finish it may bury his wife and children, as happened to יהודה.

steps.title: Why יוסף was called 'bones' in his lifetime
steps.stepSummary: רב teaches that יוסף was called 'bones' while still alive because he stayed silent when his brothers called his father 'your servant.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: Why was יוסף called 'bones' even while he was alive? Because he did not protest for his father's honor. The brothers kept saying to him 'your servant, our father,' and he said nothing at all to them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new teaching about יוסף. רב asks why יוסף talked about his own body as 'bones' while he was alive, and gives a reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יוסף made his brothers swear to carry up his 'bones,' which hints at a kind of lowering of his honor. רב says this came because יוסף heard his father יעקב called 'your servant' and did not object. Staying quiet when a parent's honor is lowered counts against a person.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
For what reason was Yosef called
'bones' during his lifetime?
phrases.notes: יוסף told his brothers to carry up 'my bones' (בראשית 50:25), calling himself 'bones' while still alive.

phrases.english: Because he did not protest for his father's honor,
for they said to him, 'your servant, our father,'
phrases.notes: בראשית 43:28 and 44:31. The brothers did not yet know he was יוסף.

phrases.english: and he did not say anything to them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: מִפְּנֵי מָה נִקְרָא יוֹסֵף עֲצָמוֹת בְּחַיָּיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the teachings about יהודה to a new set of teachings about יוסף.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יוסף was called 'bones' in his lifetime because he did not protest when his father was called 'your servant.'

steps.title: Why יוסף died before his brothers
steps.stepSummary: A second teaching says יוסף died before his brothers because he carried himself with authority.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יהודה said in the name of רב, and some say it was רבי חמא ברבי חנינא: Why did יוסף die before his brothers? Because he acted with authority, like a ruler.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another teaching about יוסף from the same speaker. It asks why יוסף died before his brothers and gives a reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumes that יוסף died first, which we see because he asked his brothers to take care of his burial. The answer is that acting with power and authority can shorten a person's life. The גמרא also notes there are two versions of who said this.

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said that Rav said,
and some say it was Rabbi Chama son of Rabbi Chanina:

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי מָה מֵת יוֹסֵף קוֹדֶם לְאֶחָיו —
phrases.english: For what reason did Yosef die before his brothers?
Because he conducted himself with authority.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי חָמָא בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching about יוסף, mostly from the same speaker as step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יוסף died before his brothers because he acted with authority.

steps.title: יוסף 'brought down' פרעה's astrologers
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר reads 'הורד' (was brought down) as 'הוריד' (brought down others): יוסף lowered פרעה's astrologers from their high position.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says, 'And יוסף was brought down to Egypt.' רבי אלעזר said: Do not read it as 'was brought down' but as 'brought down,' because יוסף brought down פרעה's astrologers from their greatness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a פסוק about יוסף going down to Egypt, and רבי אלעזר reads the word in a new way. Instead of יוסף being lowered, יוסף lowered others.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier (step 9) יהודה 'went down' from his greatness, and here a similar word is used for יוסף. רבי אלעזר changes the vowels so that יוסף is the one acting. Because יוסף could explain פרעה's dreams and the astrologers could not, they lost their high standing.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not read it as (a reading with different vowels)

steps.confusionAlert: 'אל תיקרי' does not mean the פסוק's text is changed. It means we learn an extra lesson by reading the same letters with different vowels.

phrases.english: 'And Yosef was brought down to Egypt.'
phrases.notes: בראשית 39:1.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
Do not read 'was brought down' but rather 'brought down,'
for he brought down Pharaoh's astrologers from their greatness.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״וְיוֹסֵף הוּרַד מִצְרָיְמָה״. אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: אַל תִּיקְרֵי ״הוּרַד״ אֶלָּא ״הוֹרִיד״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the teachings about יוסף, and echoes the 'going down' of יהודה in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'הורד' is read as 'הוריד': יוסף lowered Pharaoh's astrologers from their high position.

steps.title: Why פוטיפר bought יוסף and why his name changed
steps.stepSummary: רב explains that פוטיפר bought יוסף for his own sinful purpose, but angels injured him to stop it, and that is why his name changes from פוטיפר to פוטיפרע.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says, 'And פוטיפר, פרעה's סריס, bought him.' רב said: He bought him for himself. An angel came and castrated him, and גבריאל came and mutilated him further. At first the פסוק writes 'פוטיפר,' and in the end it writes 'פוטיפרע.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the same פסוק and רב explains the word 'סריס' and the change in פוטיפר's name. He uses the name change as a hint to what happened to פוטיפר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב says פוטיפר bought the handsome יוסף for an immoral purpose, but was stopped when angels injured him. The word סריס hints at castration, and the extra letter ע in the later name 'פוטיפרע' hints at 'פירעו,' a further injury. So the change in the name is the proof for רב's teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: An officer; also a castrated man
Mutilated him further (sounds like the end of 'פוטיפרע')

steps.whatToRemember: This set of teachings about יוסף shows both his weak points (not protecting his father's honor, acting with authority) and his greatness (lowering פרעה's astrologers, being protected from פוטיפר).

phrases.english: 'And Potiphar, Pharaoh's officer, bought him,'
phrases.notes: Same פסוק, בראשית 39:1.

phrases.english: Rav said: He bought him for himself.
phrases.notes: He means פוטיפר wanted יוסף for an immoral, forbidden purpose.

phrases.english: Michael came and castrated him,
phrases.notes: The printed גמרא says גבריאל in round brackets; the corrected wording in square brackets says מיכאל did this first part.

phrases.english: Gavriel came and mutilated him.
At first it is written 'Potiphar,'
and in the end, 'Potiphera.'
phrases.notes: בראשית 41:45. The added ע hints at 'פירעו,' the second injury.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״וַיִּקְנֵהוּ פּוֹטִיפַר סְרִיס פַּרְעֹה״, אָמַר רַב: שֶׁקְּנָאוֹ לְעַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the same פסוק (בראשית 39:1) begun in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פוטיפר bought יוסף for a sinful purpose and was injured by angels; the change from פוטיפר to פוטיפרע hints at this.

steps.title: משה used the word 'רב' and was answered with 'רב'
steps.stepSummary: After quoting the משנה, רבי לוי teaches that משה used the word 'רב' against קרח's group, so הקב״ה used the same word 'רב' to refuse his request.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'Who is greater to us than משה, etc.' The פסוק says: 'And ה׳ said to me: רב לך (enough for you).' רבי לוי says: He announced with 'רב', and he was told with 'רב'. He announced with 'רב': 'רב לכם, you take too much upon yourselves.' He was told with 'רב': 'רב לך, enough for you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's words about משה. רבי לוי explains why הקב״ה chose the word 'רב' when refusing משה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה once rebuked קרח's group with 'רב לכם'. The same word was later used against him, 'רב לך', when he asked to enter ארץ ישראל. This fits the theme of the פרק: a person is measured by the same measure he used.

keyTerms.meaning: They announced to him; it was proclaimed to him
You take too much upon yourselves (said to קרח's group)

phrases.english: Who, to us, is greater than Moses, etc.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from our משנה. The גמרא is now going to discuss that line.

phrases.english: "And the Lord said to me: Enough for you"
phrases.notes: דברים 3:26

phrases.english: Rabbi Levi says:
With "rav" he proclaimed, with "rav" it was proclaimed to him.
With "rav" he proclaimed: "You take too much upon you."
phrases.notes: במדבר 16:7. משה said this to קרח and his group.

phrases.english: With "rav" it was proclaimed to him: "Enough for you."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי לֵוִי: בְּ״רַב״ בִּישֵּׂר, בְּ״רַב״ בִּישְּׂרוּהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the יוסף teachings and returns to the משנה's statement about משה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה was refused with the word 'רב' because he had used 'רב' to rebuke קרח's group: measure for measure.

steps.title: Second reading: you now have a master, יהושע
steps.stepSummary: A second explanation reads 'רב לך' as 'you have a רב', a master, meaning יהושע, who will now lead.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: 'רב לך' means 'you have a רב (master)'. And who is he? יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second meaning of the words 'רב לך'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'רב' does not mean 'enough'. It means 'master'. הקב״ה was telling משה that leadership now passes to יהושע, so משה's time to lead is over.

keyTerms.meaning: משה's student, who will lead the people next

phrases.english: Alternatively: "Rav lakh"
means you have a master,
and who is he? Joshua.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר: ״רַב לָךְ״ — רַב יֵשׁ לְךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different reading of the same words explained in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'רב לך' means 'you now have a master', which is יהושע.

steps.title: Third reading: so people won't say the master is harsh and the student stubborn
steps.stepSummary: A third explanation: הקב״ה told משה to stop asking so people would not say 'How harsh the Master is, and how stubborn the student is.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: 'רב לך', stop asking, so that people should not say: 'How harsh is the Master, and how stubborn is the student.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third meaning of 'רב לך'. Here הקב״ה is telling משה to stop asking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If משה kept begging and הקב״ה kept refusing, onlookers might criticize both of them. The Master would look too hard and the student too pushy. So הקב״ה ended the conversation.

keyTerms.meaning: So that people should not say
Stubborn; one who keeps pushing and refuses to give up

phrases.english: Alternatively: "Enough for you,"
so that people should not say:
How harsh is the Master,
phrases.notes: "The Master" here means הקב״ה, and "the student" means משה.

phrases.english: and how stubborn is the student.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר: ״רַב לָךְ״, שֶׁלֹּא יֹאמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third reading of 'רב לך', next to steps 15 and 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה was told to stop asking so that neither הקב״ה nor משה would be criticized.

steps.title: Why was משה punished so much?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why משה, so righteous, received such a heavy punishment as not entering ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why so much?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question to set up the next step: why was משה's punishment so severe?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not being allowed into ארץ ישראל seems like a very harsh result for someone as great as משה. The גמרא wants to understand this.

phrases.english: And why so much?
phrases.notes: He means: why was משה punished so harshly that he could not enter ארץ ישראל?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל כָּךְ לָמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the severity of the refusal described in steps 15 through 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason משה, a great צדיק, was given so heavy a punishment.

steps.title: The burden matches the camel
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ישמעאל answers: 'The load matches the camel.' A great person is judged by his great level.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: According to the camel is the load.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a well-known saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A big camel carries a big load. In the same way, a great person like משה is held to a higher standard, so even a small mistake brings a big result.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in the school of רבי ישמעאל
According to the camel is the load

steps.whatToRemember: Greater people are judged more strictly. That is why משה's punishment was so heavy.

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
According to the camel is the load.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: לְפוּם גַּמְלָא שִׁיחְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A person is judged by his level. A great person carries a heavier 'load' of responsibility.

steps.title: Today my years are complete: the righteous live full years
steps.stepSummary: From the extra word 'היום' the גמרא learns that משה died on his exact 120th birthday, because הקב״ה completes the years of צדיקים to the day.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And he said to them: I am 120 years old today.' The word 'today' is not needed. It means: Today my days and years are filled. This teaches that הקב״ה completes the years of צדיקים from day to day and from month to month, as it says: 'The number of your days I will fill.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that the word 'היום' in משה's speech seems extra. It learns a lesson about צדיקים from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the word 'היום' adds nothing to the plain meaning, it must be teaching something. משה was telling the people that exactly on this day he finished 120 full years. The פסוק 'את מספר ימיך אמלא' supports this: הקב״ה fills the lifespan of צדיקים exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: There is no need for the פסוק to say
My days and years are filled

steps.whatToRemember: משה died on his exact 120th birthday. הקב״ה gives צדיקים complete years, to the exact day.

phrases.english: "And he said to them:
phrases.notes: דברים 31:2

phrases.aramaic: בֶּן מֵאָה וְעֶשְׂרִים שָׁנָה אָנֹכִי הַיּוֹם״,
phrases.english: I am a hundred and twenty years old today"
since there is no need for the verse to say "today":
today my days and years are filled.
This teaches you that the Holy One, Blessed be He,
completes the years of the righteous
from day to day and from month to month,
as it is written: "The number of your days I will fill."
phrases.notes: שמות 23:26

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁאֵין תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״הַיּוֹם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the refusal to enter ארץ ישראל to the day of משה's death.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הקב״ה completes the lifespan of צדיקים exactly, to the day. משה died on his 120th birthday.

steps.title: What does 'go out and come in' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes משה's words 'I can no longer go out and come in' and asks what they mean.
steps.simpleTranslation: משה said, 'I can no longer go out and come in.' What does 'go out and come in' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another phrase from משה's farewell speech and asks what it really means. This question sets up the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words could mean physical weakness, or something deeper. The גמרא raises the question so it can test the simple meaning first.

keyTerms.meaning: To go out and come in
What is it? What does it mean?

phrases.english: "I can no longer go out and come in."
phrases.notes: דברים 31:2

phrases.english: What is meant by "go out and come in"?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״לָצֵאת וְלָבוֹא״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the same speech of משה on his last day (step 20).
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The true meaning of 'go out and come in' in משה's statement.

steps.title: It cannot mean physical weakness
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the literal reading. The פסוקים say משה stayed strong until he died, and he climbed twelve steps in one stride.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it means he was physically unable to walk around, that is hard to accept. The פסוק says that at 120 his strength had not left him. Another פסוק says he went up הר נבו, and a ברייתא teaches that there were twelve steps there and משה crossed them all in one step.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the simple meaning, that משה was too weak to move around, and shows that it does not fit the פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two sources show that משה was physically strong. The פסוק says 'his natural force did not leave him,' and a ברייתא says he crossed twelve steps in a single stride on the day he died. So 'I can no longer go out and come in' must mean something other than bodily weakness.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (offering a possible reading in order to test it)
But isn't it written? (introduces a פסוק that challenges the idea)
His natural strength did not leave him

phrases.english: If you say it means literally going out and coming in,
but isn't it written: "And משה was a hundred and twenty years old
when he died... his natural strength had not left him,"
phrases.notes: דברים 34:7. The גמרא skips the middle words, 'his eye was not dim.'

phrases.aramaic: וּכְתִיב: ״וַיַּעַל מֹשֶׁה מֵעַרְבֹת מוֹאָב אֶל הַר נְבוֹ״,
phrases.english: and it is written: "And משה went up from the plains of מואב to Mount נבו,"
phrases.notes: דברים 34:1

phrases.aramaic: וְתַנְיָא: שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה מַעֲלוֹת הָיוּ שָׁם,
phrases.english: and a ברייתא taught: there were twelve steps there,
and משה stepped over them in one step.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵימָא לָצֵאת וְלָבֹא מַמָּשׁ, וְהָכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects the simplest answer to the question in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The literal reading that משה was physically unable to move around.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוקים and a ברייתא show that משה was at full strength on his last day, so physical weakness cannot be what he meant.

steps.title: It means Torah: the gates of wisdom were closed
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן explains that 'go out and come in' refers to Torah learning. On that day the gates of wisdom were closed to משה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יונתן: it means going out and coming in with words of Torah. This teaches that the gates of wisdom were closed off from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the real meaning: משה could no longer move freely through Torah wisdom the way he used to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since his body was still strong, the limit must have been spiritual. 'Going out and coming in' is read as moving in and out of Torah topics. On his last day, his access to that wisdom was taken away.
steps.whatToRemember: משה's 'I can no longer go out and come in' was not physical weakness. On his last day the gates of Torah wisdom were closed to him.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן:
phrases.english: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said that רבי יונתן said:
It means going out and coming in with words of Torah.
This teaches that the gates of wisdom were closed off from him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21 in a way that avoids the problem raised in step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Go out and come in' refers to Torah. The gates of wisdom were closed to משה.

steps.title: Two leaders on one שבת: leadership passes to יהושע
steps.stepSummary: From the פסוק 'משה and יהושע went and stood in the אהל מועד,' a ברייתא teaches that on משה's last שבת both led together, and authority passed from משה to יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says, 'משה and יהושע went and stood in the אהל מועד.' A ברייתא taught: that שבת had two leaders at once. Authority was taken from one and given to the other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching that on משה's final שבת, two leaders stood together and leadership was handed from משה to יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק shows משה and יהושע standing side by side. The ברייתא explains that this was the moment of transfer: משה's authority ended and יהושע's began on the same day.

keyTerms.meaning: Two pairs; two leaders serving at the same time

phrases.english: "And משה and יהושע went
and stood in the אהל מועד."
phrases.notes: דברים 31:14

phrases.english: It was taught: that שבת
was one of two pairs,
phrases.notes: In plain words, two leaders, משה and יהושע, were in charge at the same time.

phrases.english: authority was taken from this one,
and given to that one.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: אוֹתָהּ שַׁבָּת שֶׁל דְּיוֹ זוּגֵי הָיְתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from משה's words on his last day to the handover of leadership on that same day.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On משה's last שבת, authority passed from משה to יהושע.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: משה died in the portion of ראובן
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה begins a surprising teaching that could only be said because a פסוק supports it. משה died on הר נבו, and נבו is in the land of the tribe of ראובן.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא taught that רבי יהודה said: if there were no written פסוק, it would be impossible to say this. Where did משה die? In the portion of ראובן. It says 'משה went up from the plains of מואב to Mount נבו,' and נבו is in ראובן's portion, as it says 'And the children of ראובן built... and נבו.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה starts a teaching about where משה died and proves the first part from two פסוקים. His opening words show that something surprising is coming, so this step sets up what follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He links two פסוקים: משה went up to הר נבו to die, and the tribe of ראובן built נבו. Putting them together shows that משה died in ראובן's land. 'If not for a written פסוק' signals that the full teaching, which continues after this, is bold enough that only a פסוק could support it.

keyTerms.meaning: If not for a written פסוק
It would be impossible to say it
The portion (land) of the tribe of ראובן

phrases.english: And it was taught in a ברייתא that רבי יהודה said:

phrases.aramaic: אִילְמָלֵא מִקְרָא כָּתוּב, אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְאוֹמְרוֹ.
phrases.english: If not for a written פסוק, it would be impossible to say it.

phrases.aramaic: הֵיכָן מֹשֶׁה מֵת — בְּחֶלְקוֹ שֶׁל רְאוּבֵן,
phrases.english: Where did משה die? In the portion of ראובן,

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב: ״וַיַּעַל מֹשֶׁה מֵעַרְבֹת מוֹאָב אֶל הַר נְבוֹ״,
phrases.english: as it is written: "And משה went up from the plains of מואב to Mount נבו,"
and נבו is located in the portion of ראובן,

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב: ״וּבְנֵי רְאוּבֵן בָּנוּ וְגוֹ׳ וְאֶת נְבוֹ וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: as it is written: "And the children of ראובן built... and נבו..."
phrases.notes: במדבר 32:37–38. 'וגו׳' means the פסוק goes on, like 'etc.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: אִילְמָלֵא מִקְרָא כָּתוּב, אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְאוֹמְרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of משה's death by asking where it took place.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה died on הר נבו, which is in the portion of ראובן. This is proven by combining דברים 34:1 with במדבר 32:37–38.

steps.title: Why the mountain is called נבו
steps.stepSummary: The name נבו hints that three נביאים died there: משה, אהרן, and מרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is called 'נבו' because three prophets died there: משה, אהרן, and מרים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a small side point about the name of the mountain where משה died. Then it goes back to רבי יהודה's main teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word נבו sounds like נביאים (prophets). The גמרא reads the name as a hint to the three great prophets of the מדבר generation. It is a quick word-play inside the larger story.

keyTerms.meaning: Nevo, the mountain where משה died

phrases.english: "Nevo": because there died
phrases.notes: A word-play: נבו sounds like נביאים, 'prophets.'

phrases.english: three prophets:
Moshe, Aharon, and Miriam.

steps.triggerLanguage: נְבוֹ שֶׁשָּׁם מֵתוּ שְׁלֹשָׁה נְבִיאִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a short explanation of the name נבו, which was just mentioned as the place of משה's death.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The name נבו hints that three נביאים died there: משה, אהרן, and מרים.

steps.title: משה was buried in the land of גד
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק shows that משה is buried in the land of גד, four מיל away from where he died in the land of ראובן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where is משה buried? In the portion of גד, as it says: 'And he saw a first part for himself.' How far is it from the portion of ראובן to the portion of גד? Four מיל.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה shows that משה was buried in a different place from where he died. This sets up the big question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 25 we learned that משה died on הר נבו, in ראובן's land. Now a פסוק from משה's blessing to גד shows that he was buried in גד's land. The gap between the two places is four מיל, so someone had to bring him there.

keyTerms.meaning: His portion, the land given to a tribe

phrases.english: And where is Moshe buried?
In the portion of Gad,
as it is written: "And he saw a first part for himself, etc."
phrases.notes: דברים 33:21, from משה's blessing to גד.

phrases.english: And from the portion of Reuven

phrases.aramaic: עַד חֶלְקוֹ שֶׁל גָּד כַּמָּה הָוֵי —
phrases.english: to the portion of Gad, how much is it?
Four mil.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהֵיכָן מֹשֶׁה קָבוּר בְּחֶלְקוֹ שֶׁל גָּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רבי יהודה's teaching from step 25 and adds the burial place, which is different from the place of death.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה was buried in the land of גד, four מיל from נבו in the land of ראובן.

steps.title: Who carried משה the four מיל?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה asks who carried משה's body from where he died to where he was buried.
steps.simpleTranslation: Those four מיל: who carried him?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה asks the key question that the last two facts create. This sets up the surprising answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה died alone on the mountain, and no person knew where he was buried. So if he traveled four מיל after his death, no human could have carried him.

phrases.english: Those four mil:
who carried him?

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹתָן אַרְבָּעָה מִילִין מִי הוֹלִיכוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the question raised by the gap between the place of death (step 25) and the place of burial (step 27).
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who moved משה's body the four מיל from נבו to his grave in גד's land?

steps.title: משה was carried on the wings of the שכינה
steps.stepSummary: משה lay on the wings of the שכינה. The angels praised him, and הקדוש ברוך הוא mourned: 'Who will stand up for Me now?'
steps.simpleTranslation: This teaches that משה was lying on the wings of the שכינה. The ministering angels were saying, 'He did the righteousness of ה׳ and His judgments with Israel.' And הקדוש ברוך הוא was saying, 'Who will rise up for Me against evildoers? Who will stand up for Me against workers of wrongdoing?'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה answers that הקדוש ברוך הוא Himself carried משה to his grave. On the way, the angels praised משה and הקדוש ברוך הוא mourned him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the surprising teaching that step 25 promised, the one we could only say because the פסוקים force it. Death in ראובן's land plus burial in גד's land means someone carried him, and the answer is the שכינה. The angels quote the end of the same פסוק about גד, and הקדוש ברוך הוא asks who will now defend Israel the way משה did.

keyTerms.meaning: The wings of the Divine Presence

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how strongly the גמרא relies on a פסוק before saying something this bold about הקדוש ברוך הוא.

phrases.english: This teaches that Moshe was
lying on the wings of the Divine Presence,
and the ministering angels were saying:
"He did the righteousness of ה׳,
and His judgments with Israel,"
phrases.notes: The end of the same פסוק about גד, דברים 33:21.

phrases.english: and the Holy One, Blessed be He, was saying:
"Who will rise up for Me against evildoers?

phrases.aramaic: מִי יִתְיַצֵּב לִי עִם פּוֹעֲלֵי אָוֶן״.
phrases.english: Who will stand up for Me against workers of wrongdoing?"
phrases.notes: תהלים 94:16. He means: now that משה is gone, who will defend Israel?

steps.triggerLanguage: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁהָיָה מֹשֶׁה מוּטָּל בְּכַנְפֵי שְׁכִינָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 28 and completes רבי יהודה's teaching begun in step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: הקדוש ברוך הוא Himself carried משה on the wings of the שכינה, while the angels praised משה and הקדוש ברוך הוא mourned him.

steps.title: Other views of what ה׳ said in mourning משה
steps.stepSummary: שמואל, רבי יוחנן, רב נחמן, and סמליון each give a different line that הקדוש ברוך הוא said when משה died.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: 'Who is like the wise man, and who knows the meaning of a matter?' רבי יוחנן said: 'Wisdom, where can it be found?' רב נחמן said: 'And משה died there.' סמליון said: 'And משה died there, the great scribe of Israel.'
steps.whatsHappening: Several אמוראים offer other words that הקדוש ברוך הוא said while mourning משה, instead of the פסוק from תהלים in the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each view stresses a different side of משה's greatness. שמואל points to his wisdom in understanding matters, and רבי יוחנן says such wisdom can no longer be found. רב נחמן quotes the plain פסוק of his death, and סמליון adds the title 'the great scribe of Israel.'

keyTerms.meaning: The great scribe, the great teacher of Torah

steps.whatToRemember: משה died on נבו in ראובן's land but was buried in גד's land. הקדוש ברוך הוא Himself carried him there and mourned him. The אמוראים offer different words for that mourning.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
"Who is like the wise man,
and who knows the meaning of a matter?"
phrases.notes: קהלת 8:1.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
"Wisdom, where can it be found?"
phrases.notes: איוב 28:12.

phrases.english: And Rav Nachman said:
"And Moshe died there, etc."
Semalyon said:
"And Moshe died there,
the great scribe of Israel."
phrases.notes: סמליון adds these Aramaic words to the פסוק's description of משה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר מִי כְּהֶחָכָם וּמִי יוֹדֵעַ פֵּשֶׁר דָּבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers other versions of the words הקדוש ברוך הוא said, in place of the פסוק quoted in step 29.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Different אמוראים hold that הקדוש ברוך הוא mourned משה with different words: about his wisdom, about wisdom being lost, about his death, or calling him the great scribe of Israel.

steps.title: A heavenly voice announces משה's death across the camp
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר הגדול teaches that a בת קול announced 'משה, the great scribe of ישראל, has died' over an area of twelve מיל by twelve מיל, the size of the camp of ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches that רבי אליעזר הגדול says: Over an area of twelve מיל by twelve מיל, the size of the camp of ישראל, a heavenly voice called out: 'משה, the great scribe of ישראל, has died.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא describing how the whole nation heard the news of משה's death through a heavenly voice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The voice covered exactly the area of the camp of ישראל, so every single Jew heard it. משה is called 'ספרא רבה', the great scribe, because he was the one who taught the Torah to ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: A measure of distance, roughly a kilometer
The camp of the Jewish people in the desert
The great scribe, meaning the great teacher of Torah

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Eliezer the Great says:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר מִיל עַל שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר מִיל,
phrases.english: Over twelve mil by twelve mil,
matching the size of the camp of Israel,
a heavenly voice called out and said:
"And Moses, the great scribe of Israel, died."

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הַגָּדוֹל אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the description of what happened when משה died, adding how ישראל heard the news.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בת קול announced משה's death over the entire area of the camp of ישראל.

steps.title: Some say משה did not really die
steps.stepSummary: Some say משה never actually died. The word 'שם' appears both in 'he died there' and in 'he was there with ה׳'. Just as in the second פסוק he stood and served ה׳, so too here he is standing and serving ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: משה did not die. It says here, 'And he died there', and it says elsewhere, 'And he was there with ה׳'. Just as there he was standing and serving, so too here he is standing and serving.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different opinion: משה's 'death' was really a move to standing and serving ה׳ forever. It learns this by comparing the same word 'שם' in two פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a גזירה שוה. The word 'שם' links the פסוק about משה's death to the פסוק about his forty days on הר סיני. Since on סיני 'there' meant standing before ה׳ and serving Him, the 'there' of his death is read the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: It is written here... and it is written there: the formula for comparing two פסוקים
Learning from the same word appearing in two places

steps.confusionAlert: This opinion does not say the פסוק 'וימת' is wrong. It explains what that 'death' really was: משה continues to stand and serve before ה׳.

phrases.english: And some say: Moses did not die,
as it is written here: "And he died there,"
phrases.notes: דברים 34:5

phrases.english: and it is written there: "And he was there with the Lord,"
phrases.notes: שמות 34:28. This is about משה's forty days on הר סיני.

phrases.english: just as there he was standing and serving,
so too here he is standing and serving.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: לֹא מֵת מֹשֶׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different view of the death that was just announced: it was not a death in the usual sense.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Through a גזירה שוה on 'שם', משה's 'death' means he stands and serves before ה׳.

steps.title: An exact burial location, yet no one knows the grave
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק gives a very detailed location: in the valley, in the land of מואב, opposite בית פעור. רבי ברכיה notes this is 'a sign within a sign', yet the פסוק still says no one knows where משה is buried.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And He buried him in the valley in the land of מואב, opposite בית פעור.' רבי ברכיה said: This is a sign within a sign, and even so, 'no man knows his burial place'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the פסוק about משה's burial. רבי ברכיה points out a surprising contrast in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק stacks one landmark on top of another (valley, מואב, opposite בית פעור), which should make the grave easy to find. Even with all these clues, the same פסוק says no one knows the grave. The grave stays hidden in spite of the exact address.

keyTerms.meaning: A place in מואב named after the idol פעור
A sign within a sign: a very precise description

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the story that comes next, which shows how hard it really is to find משה's grave.

phrases.english: "And He buried him in the valley
phrases.notes: דברים 34:6

phrases.english: in the land of Moab, opposite Beth Peor."

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי בֶּרֶכְיָה: סִימָן בְּתוֹךְ סִימָן,
phrases.english: Rabbi Berekhya said: A sign within a sign,
phrases.notes: He means the פסוק piles up landmarks, so the location sounds very exact.

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲפִילּוּ הָכִי: ״וְלֹא יָדַע אִישׁ אֶת קְבֻרָתוֹ״.
phrases.english: and even so: "And no man knows his burial place."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי בֶּרֶכְיָה: סִימָן בְּתוֹךְ סִימָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from משה's death to his burial place, returning to the burial theme of step 27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Although the פסוק describes the burial place very precisely, no one knows where משה's grave is.

steps.title: The Roman government sends messengers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a story: the wicked Roman government once sent messengers to... The story continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the wicked government (Rome) already once sent to...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a story that will show how no one can find משה's grave. This line only sets up the story, which finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'וכבר' (and already, once) signals a real event that backs up רבי ברכיה's point. The story will show the 'no one knows his grave' of the פסוק in action.

keyTerms.meaning: And already, once (introduces a past event)
The wicked government, meaning the Roman Empire

phrases.english: And the wicked government already once sent to

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְבָר שָׁלְחָה מַלְכוּת הָרְשָׁעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a story that illustrates the hidden grave described in step 33.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A story begins about the Roman government sending messengers, which will show that משה's grave cannot be found.
